6. **U6**: Documentation on "direct binding" for s-c-d

8. **U8**: Tap support in s-c-dataflow DSL/Shell

technical_and_design_decisions: Use Apache Geode (Pivotal Gemfire) Java client API as the foundation for all Gemfire integrations; target a recent Gemfire/Geode 1.x release for the binder and SPI.

Follow existing Spring Cloud Stream binder patterns (Kafka/RabbitMQ style) when implementing the Gemfire message-channel binder, including partitioned, consumer-group, and dead-letter-equivalent behavior.
Implement the binder using Gemfire client/server topology: a client cache with regions for P2P messaging and CQ/async listeners for pub-sub style consumption.
Model the Gemfire SPI as a thin adapter layer on top of Spring Cloud Data Flow's existing SPI contracts so that Gemfire implementations of repository and registry are pluggable.
Use Gemfire regions (with appropriate key design, e.g., REPLICATE/PR) for the stream repository and module registry to satisfy durability and lookup patterns.
Model the 'tap' feature as a first-class named stream construct (tap:stream-name > destination) integrated with the existing stream deployer rather than at the binder level.
Extend the existing Spring Cloud Data Flow DSL parser (Fluent DSL) to recognize the new 'tap' keyword, and expose equivalent commands in the Spring Cloud Data Flow Shell.
Use Spring Boot auto-configuration for Gemfire client beans so that Gemfire integration is enabled via standard Spring Cloud Stream/Data Flow configuration properties.
Documentation will follow existing Spring Cloud reference-guide style (Asciidoctor), use the code example in U6 verbatim, and provide partition/deployment-manifest snippets for U5.
assumptions: Java 17+ is the target JDK, consistent with Spring Framework 6.0 requirements.
A single experienced developer performs all the work; the developer is already familiar with the Spring Cloud Stream and Spring Cloud Data Flow codebases.

Test infrastructure (unit tests + integration tests against an embedded or local Gemfire locator/server) is available; no significant time is needed to bring up new CI infrastructure beyond configuration.
The 'direct binding' (U6) and 'partition documentation' (U5) work is purely documentation; no new runtime code is required beyond review of existing behavior to ensure examples are accurate.
The 'tap' feature (U7, U8) is implemented at the dataflow/stream-deployer level and is binder-agnostic; it does not require per-binder changes.
The Gemfire binder does not need to implement advanced Gemfire features (transactions, WAN replication, PDX serialization with custom types) beyond what is needed for typical messaging use cases.
All estimates are 'most likely' effort in workdays (8-hour productive day) for one developer, exclusive of meetings and unrelated overhead.
Effort includes design, implementation, unit tests, and integration tests for each activity, but not separate formal QA or product management work.

activities.activity_description: Bootstrap new Maven modules for the Gemfire binder, SPI, repository, and registry; add Gemfire/Geode client dependencies; configure Spring Boot auto-configuration; set up an embedded/local Gemfire locator for integration tests; wire CI build profiles.

Develop the Spring Cloud Stream binder for Gemfire: producer/consumer abstractions, partitioned and consumer-group support, configuration properties, message conversion, error handling, and integration with Gemfire regions and async listeners. Includes unit and integration tests.

activities.activity_name: Implement Gemfire SPI for Spring Cloud Data Flow (U2)
activities.activity_description: Define and implement the Gemfire-backed implementations of the Data Flow SPI interfaces so that data microservices can be orchestrated against a Gemfire cluster. Includes design of the SPI contract extensions and integration tests against a real Gemfire locator.

Build the stream definition repository on top of Gemfire regions: CRUD for stream definitions, schema/versioning, query APIs, and integration with the Data Flow server. Include persistence, eviction policy choices, and tests.

Build the module registry on top of Gemfire regions: registration of module coordinates, lookup-by-name and lookup-by-type APIs, caching behavior, and integration tests covering concurrent registration and lookup.

activities.activity_name: Document deployment manifest with focus on partitions (U5)
activities.activity_description: Author/reference documentation describing how to configure Spring Cloud Data Flow deployment manifests with respect to partitions for streams. Include concrete manifest snippets, partition count guidance, and a worked example for a partitioned Gemfire-backed stream.

activities.activity_name: Document 'direct binding' for Spring Cloud Data Flow (U6)
activities.activity_description: Write documentation for the direct-binding feature in Spring Cloud Data Flow, including the provided example invocation of spring-cloud-stream-module-launcher, explanation of --modules, --args, --aggregate and binding flags, and edge cases.

activities.activity_name: Implement tap support in the stream pipeline (U7)
activities.activity_description: Design and implement the runtime mechanism that allows a named tap to fork a primary stream's data to one or more destinations without impacting the original stream. Update the stream deployer, deployment model, and lifecycle handling; add integration tests for fan-out behavior.

activities.activity_name: Add tap support to s-c-dataflow DSL and Shell (U8)
activities.activity_description: Extend the Spring Cloud Data Flow Fluent DSL to accept the 'tap' construct, update the parser/validator, and add the corresponding shell command. Include end-to-end tests verifying that a DSL/shell-defined tap deploys correctly.

activities.activity_name: Cross-feature integration testing and bug fixing
activities.activity_description: Run end-to-end integration scenarios combining the Gemfire binder, SPI, repository, registry, and tap feature (DSL + shell). Fix defects found, harden error handling, and verify no regressions against existing binders and repositories.

activities.activity_name: Final documentation polish, review and release preparation
activities.activity_description: Final pass over reference and user-guide documentation, update release notes, ensure consistent examples, verify Maven coordinates, and prepare the release artifacts (sample apps, BOM updates).
